SCALED FROM A MEASURED NUMBER, and the scaling is stated so it can be checked: T20's 240-cell 3000-step chtMultiRegionFoam solid-only case cost a MEASURED 0.017 core-min (1.02 core-s), i.e. 0.34 ms per step at 240 cells. T25_MOD_L1 is 960 cells (4.0x) and 1800 steps (0.6x), giving 2.4 core-s of solve by linear scaling; the POINT is set to 1.0 core-min (60 core-s), ~25x that, because per-step cost is NOT the dominant term here -- this case writes 180 field sets and runs a probes function object EVERY time step (1800 probe writes), and T20's own feasibility probe measured 90.7 percent of its wall time as startup and I/O rather than solving (T20_LC_FEAS: 3 s wall against 0.28 s ExecutionTime). The I/O term, not the cell count, is what this estimate is guessing at, and it is a GUESS: this is the lab's first 8-block multi-patch chtMultiRegionFoam case and no measured I/O rate exists for it. CAP 10.0 core-min hard = 10x POINT (timeout 600 wall s at 1 rank); the headroom is deliberate and reflects that the POINT rests on an unmeasured I/O term. An overrun STOPS THE RUN and does not get a new budget (CLAUDE.md rule 12).
